title: Coming to Unity from web/backend dev, What was the thing that almost made you quit?
author: AnarchyDex
selftext:
Full-stack dev here. C# was the easy part the language is fine, the tooling around it is fine. What got me was Unity as a development environment. The disconnect between code and runtime state. The way half the actual game logic lives in scene files and prefabs as serialized data instead of code, so reading the codebase tells you almost nothing about how the game actually behaves. Domain reload wiping your state every time you hit play. Scene and prefab merges in git being their own special hell. Tutorials that were correct in 2022 referencing APIs that don't exist anymore. The render pipeline mess picking URP vs HDRP vs Built-in feels like choosing which set of broken tutorials you want to use. AssetDatabase quirks where you touch a file the wrong way and corrupt your project's metadata. 

None of this is "Unity is hard to learn." It's more like Unity has its own way of doing everything and a lot of it actively fights how I'd build software anywhere else. 

Curious if other devs from other stacks (web, backend, mobile, ML) had the same experience. What was the moment you nearly bailed? Did you push through?

replies.body: To be gonetr. I haven't. For the time being teasing the gameplay mechanics i want I just did em in html/J's using react and three.js and such. The aibhad a much easier time pulling that off than arguign with it. Once my prototypes were functional I was trying to convert them over to c#

comments.author: Melodic-Chemistry127
comments.body:
I ended up hating Unity's UI systems so much, I switched to Godot. Each of the systems has different feature sets, the new one they're pushing(UI Toolkit) is still feature incomplete compared to previous systems. It's a bunch of hot garbage and I don't understand how people are putting up with it.

I come from a similar background as you and it was jarring how bad Unity was compared to the quality of tooling I was used to. It's almost like going twenty years back in time.

comments.author: GDEmerald
comments.body:
UI mostly. Working with SolidJS/Signal based frameworks full time and then having to deal with INotifyPropertyChanged like it's 2014 WPF again, was not working for me. + UI Toolkit is not compareable to JS UI Frameworks.


Also Hot Reload. I do not have the time waiting 5+ seconds every time I change something....


Last thing also what you pointed out: Learning unity specific stuff I will not need anywhere else was rough, so I mostly sticked to what I knew, which lead to different problems.


Now I am doing my own typescript/signal based ECS with a roguelike attached. Probably is overkill, but at least I learn something new.
